faq.description: A practical overview of how Contrazy fits real contract and payment workflows.

items.q: Does Contrazy replace my existing contract text?
items.a: No. Your legal content stays yours. Contrazy structures the workflow around review, signature, KYC, deposit, and payment steps.

items.q: Can I use it without KYC?
items.a: Yes. KYC can remain optional and only be enabled for workflows that need stronger identity verification.
Deposits can be authorized as card holds, then later released or captured depending on the outcome of the transaction.
No. Clients follow the secure link or QR code you send them and complete the guided journey without needing a vendor dashboard login.

items.q: Can internal teams review disputes and onboarding states?
items.a: Yes. Admin and vendor views separate operational oversight from the customer-facing flow.

terms.title: Terms & Conditions
terms.description: These terms outline the framework for using Contrazy as a transaction workflow platform.

sections.title: Platform scope
paragraphs: Contrazy provides workflow tooling for contracts, identity checks, signatures, deposits, and payments.
Use of the platform does not replace your own legal, accounting, or regulatory obligations.

sections.title: Account responsibilities
paragraphs: You are responsible for the accuracy of business information, payment setup, and the workflows you send to customers.
You must protect access credentials and restrict workspace access to authorised team members.

sections.title: Customer-facing content
paragraphs: You remain responsible for the agreements, instructions, and business terms you publish through Contrazy.
Contrazy does not automatically validate that your workflow content is legally sufficient for your market.
bullets: Keep support and payout information current.

privacy.metaDescription: Read how Contrazy handles personal data and operational records.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: This overview explains how Contrazy processes account, workflow, and transaction data.

sections.title: Data processed
paragraphs: Contrazy processes account details, workflow configuration, transaction records, and customer-submitted information needed for the service.
Additional processors such as Stripe may handle payment or identity data within their own systems.

sections.title: Why data is used
paragraphs: We use data to operate the platform, secure workflows, support payments, and provide operational visibility.
We also use limited operational logs to monitor incidents and improve service reliability.

sections.title: Retention and access
paragraphs: Data is retained according to service needs, legal obligations, and operational requirements.
Access is restricted by role so vendors and administrators only see records relevant to their responsibilities.

imprint.metaDescription: Legal notice and publishing information for Contrazy.
imprint.title: Legal Notice
imprint.description: Publishing and company information for Contrazy.

sections.title: Publisher
paragraphs: Contrazy is presented as a secure transaction workflow platform for vendors and operations teams.

sections.title: Contact
paragraphs: For corporate, support, or legal questions, use the contact channels listed in the application contact page.

sections.title: Hosting and processors
paragraphs: Infrastructure and processing services may rely on third-party providers for hosting, payments, storage, and verification workflows.

gdpr.metaDescription: GDPR-related information for Contrazy platform usage and data handling.
gdpr.title: GDPR
gdpr.description: A practical summary of how Contrazy supports GDPR-minded operations.

sections.title: Roles and responsibilities
paragraphs: Depending on the workflow, customers, vendors, and service providers may each have different data protection roles.
Vendors are responsible for ensuring they have an appropriate legal basis for the data they collect through Contrazy.

sections.title: Security measures
paragraphs: Contrazy uses role-based access, secure transport, and processor integrations designed for production use.
Sensitive payment and identity operations are delegated to specialised providers where appropriate.

sections.title: Requests and governance
paragraphs: Data subject requests should be handled according to your organisation's own privacy process and applicable law.
Keep internal retention, access, and support procedures aligned with the workflows you operate.
